options.text: A private registry for storing (and building) container images

questions.explanation: ACR is Azure's private container registry for storing images; it can also build images in the cloud with `az acr build`. Container services pull images from it.

questions.prompt: Which statements about container services are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: ACI runs single containers serverlessly, billed per second
Container Apps is serverless and can scale to zero
AKS is managed Kubernetes for full orchestration control
AKS is the simplest option with the least operational overhead

questions.explanation: ACI runs single containers; Container Apps is serverless with scale-to-zero; AKS is managed Kubernetes. AKS has the MOST operational overhead, not the least.

questions.prompt: The serverless platform for containers and microservices that can scale to zero is Azure Container ____.
questions.explanation: Azure Container Apps is a serverless container platform (built on Kubernetes + KEDA) with autoscaling including scale-to-zero, ingress, and revisions.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to run a container on Azure.

items.text: Deploy it to a container service

questions.explanation: Build the image, push it to a registry like ACR, then deploy it to ACI, Container Apps, or AKS.

questions.prompt: Match each service to what it's best for.

pairs.right: A single container, run and go

questions.explanation: ACI = single containers; Container Apps = serverless microservices; AKS = full Kubernetes; ACR = image storage.
